policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 14:21 reads 'he that hath pity on the poor' with no note attached to this unit. 'The poor' does not distinguish qere ענוים (humble/afflicted) from ketiv עניים (poor/afflicted): the ASV renders both lemmas with 'poor' elsewhere in Proverbs, and the English carries no sense of meekness that would pick the qere nor of destitution that would pick the ketiv. Both readings remain permitted; the qere base fallback carries the projection.
